# Training budgets: change the data, the update direction, or the comparison?

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/foundation-models/training-budget.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-27 · 28 topic entries / 6 representative comparisons

Better training within one budget can come from data mixtures, per-example editing, update quality, or lower state costs. DoReMi, Mixing Laws, DataOrchestra, Muon, and ECO act at different points. Muon Paired Budget freezes model selection and asks equal-data and equal-time questions separately.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Sampling a domain more often differs from rewriting its examples

DoReMi adjusts domain frequency using excess loss, and Mixing Laws predicts mixtures from pilots. DataOrchestra chooses whether and how to edit each chunk, changing supervision. More cleaned text or lower mean loss does not guarantee target gains. Isolate data volume, content, and preprocessing cost; specify whether raw tokens, processed tokens, or steps are fixed.

Sources: [DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining](../../../../reproductions/2305.10429-doremi/README-en.md) · [Data Mixing Laws: Optimizing Data Mixtures by Predicting Language Modeling Performance](../../../../reproductions/2403.16952-data-mixing-laws/README-en.md) · [DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data](../../../../reproductions/2607.24717-data-orchestra/README-en.md)

### The budget can reverse the conclusion

Muon changes update direction; ECO changes persistent state and quantized updates. Both can change step time. Paired Budget separates equal-data and equal-time comparisons with frozen development choices, avoiding a new champion per report. Count auxiliary AdamW, preprocessing, and pilots. Formulas and synthetic curves verify accounting only, not actual training efficiency.

Sources: [Muon is Scalable for LLM Training](../../../../reproductions/2502.16982-muon/README-en.md) · [ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights](../../../../foundation-models/2601.22101-eco-optimizer/README-en.md) · [When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark](../../../../foundation-models/2610.21555-muon-paired-budget/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why can DoReMi upweighting and DataOrchestra cleaning change a difficult domain in opposite ways? {#cross-mixture-versus-rewrite}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** DoReMi samples more from domains underfit relative to a reference, assuming their contents are useful. DataOrchestra may drop, retain, or rewrite chunks. Upweighting can repeat noise, and aggressive cleaning can remove clean signal. Diagnose the issue and compare equal budgets.

    **Illustrative example:** Rare correct equations can merit more exposure despite high excess loss, whereas corrupted text should be cleaned rather than sampled more.

    Sources: [DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining](../../../../reproductions/2305.10429-doremi/README-en.md) · [DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data](../../../../reproductions/2607.24717-data-orchestra/README-en.md)

### How do DoReMi and Data Mixing Laws differ in assumptions when choosing large-model mixtures from small runs? {#cross-proxy-feedback-versus-law}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** DoReMi assumes proxy excess-loss dynamics identify worthwhile domains. Mixing Laws assumes pilot proportions and scales sufficiently fit a loss surface for untested combinations. Proxy-target differences can break either. Record pilot costs and evaluate the target independently rather than reporting fitted scores as training.

    **Illustrative example:** A proxy may underfit code that a large model already understands, and fitted curves may fail at extreme mixtures.

    Sources: [DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining](../../../../reproductions/2305.10429-doremi/README-en.md) · [Data Mixing Laws: Optimizing Data Mixtures by Predicting Language Modeling Performance](../../../../reproductions/2403.16952-data-mixing-laws/README-en.md)

### Why doesn't lower Muon loss at equal tokens prove a win under fixed training time? {#cross-equal-steps-versus-time}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Tokens control data exposure, not orthogonalization, auxiliary AdamW, or throughput. Compare validation on the shared observed time range using frozen development choices. Measure ECO's state savings separately, since smaller state need not mean faster steps.

    **Illustrative example:** A more effective but twice as slow update may lose to one that sees more data in the same hour.

    Sources: [Muon is Scalable for LLM Training](../../../../reproductions/2502.16982-muon/README-en.md) · [When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark](../../../../foundation-models/2610.21555-muon-paired-budget/README-en.md) · [ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights](../../../../foundation-models/2601.22101-eco-optimizer/README-en.md)
